name: Bellows guidewire
full_name: Soft fluidic bellows guidewire with teleoperated drive and imitation-learning policy
group: Krieger lab, Johns Hopkins, with Sochol (University of Maryland)
devices_driven: own 3D-printed fluid-driven soft robot, 5 mm bellows (large-scale analogue of a microguidewire, not a clinical size)
force_sensing: force sensor in leader handle only (teleoperation); none on follower
haptics_leader: no force feedback; operator pushes a force-sensing handle, forces map proportionally to bend and translate velocity
imaging_compat: overhead camera converted to simulated fluoroscopy; no real X-ray
validation_detail: 36 training mazes from 1584 possible, rearranged test set 3 mazes, novel test set 3 mazes; 647 demonstrations (218 normal, 429 recovery incl. DAgger)
key_numbers: 83 % success on unseen layouts, 75 % on unseen patient-derived geometry (abstract); ablations 22 % to 61 % success; segmentation tip error 0.6 mm median, 1.9 mm 95th, 8.0 mm max
sim_model: no physics model; only a fluoroscopy rendering of camera frames (Sec. III-B)
sim2real_detail: none found: the policy trains on real teleoperated demonstrations with simulated fluoroscopy images; the paper contrasts itself with digital-twin-trained policies
